hints: Consider the two connected particles as a single system of total mass $0.5 + 0.3 = 0.8\text{ kg}$ moving with common upward acceleration $a$.
Apply Newton's second law to the whole system: $F_{\text{up}} - (m_P + m_Q)g = (m_P + m_Q)a$, and solve for $a$.
Isolate particle $Q$ (mass $0.3\text{ kg}$) with forces tension $T$ upwards and weight $0.3g$ downwards: $T - 0.3g = 0.3a$, and solve for $T$.
walkthrough:
Identify the forces acting on the two connected particles:
- For particle $P$ ($m_P = 0.5\text{ kg}$): upward external force $10\text{ N}$, downward weight $W_P = 0.5g = 5\text{ N}$, and downward tension $T$ from the string connecting it to $Q$.
- For particle $Q$ ($m_Q = 0.3\text{ kg}$): upward tension $T$ from the string, and downward weight $W_Q = 0.3g = 3\text{ N}$.

Consider the combined system of mass $M = m_P + m_Q = 0.5 + 0.3 = 0.8\text{ kg}$ moving with common vertical acceleration $a$:
The internal tension forces cancel. Apply Newton's second law vertically upwards:
$$\sum F_{\text{up}} = M a$$
$$10 - (m_P + m_Q)g = (m_P + m_Q)a$$
Substitute $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$10 - (0.8)(10) = 0.8a$$
$$10 - 8 = 0.8a$$
$$2 = 0.8a$$
Divide both sides by $0.8$:
$$a = \frac{2}{0.8} = \frac{20}{8} = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Isolate particle $Q$ to determine the tension $T$ in the string:
Particle $Q$ accelerates upwards at $a = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Apply Newton's second law to $Q$:
$$\sum F_{\text{up}} = m_Q a$$
$$T - m_Q g = m_Q a$$
Substitute $m_Q = 0.3\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $a = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T - (0.3)(10) = (0.3)(2.5)$$
$$T - 3 = 0.75$$
Add $3$ to both sides:
$$T = 3 + 0.75 = 3.75\text{ N}$$
Thus, the upward acceleration is $2.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the tension in the string is $3.75\text{ N}$.
